recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No further core FHIR source work is needed for FHIR-13890 unless a future Patient Care decision changes AdverseEvent.subject target profiles or the group usage guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-13890 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care STU3 change request asking for AdverseEvent.subject to include Group, with a usage note saying that if AdverseEvent.resultingCondition differs among members of the group then Patient should be used as the subject.
initial_application: Historical commit 32b35437cc8daef171fb42950801c6a39d6f918b explicitly included '#13890 - add AdverseEvent.subject Reference(Group)' and changed the then-authoritative AdverseEvent spreadsheet source from Reference(Patient|ResearchSubject|Practitioner|RelatedPerson) to Reference(Patient|Group|Practitioner|RelatedPerson), added the requested comment, and recorded GF#13890.
additional_context: AdverseEvent is active in source/fhir.ini. The current XML StructureDefinition retains GF#13890, includes Group as a subject target, and updates the usage note from resultingCondition to the current element name resultingEffect. Later same-area work such as FHIR-13893, FHIR-13891, FHIR-34316, and FHIR-40657 preserved Group support while changing cardinality, removing ResearchSubject, or renaming resultingCondition/resultingEffect.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current authoritative source already implements the Jira request and no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence was found.
